prefs.name: Foldkit skill synchronization
prefs.description: Public API and ownership changes keep the published Foldkit skill current.
prefs.question: Does this change rename, remove, or reshape a public API, change a package's ownership boundary, or add a package without making the corresponding update required in skills/foldkit-plus?
prefs.guidance: Review the whole diff. A rename, removal, or shape change to an exported API requires an update to the matching reference file. An ownership change requires matching skill guidance. A new package requires both the package table entry in SKILL.md and coverage in a reference file. Do not count internal-only changes or backwards-compatible additions to an existing package unless they change its documented ownership boundary.

prefs.name: Application transition bypass
prefs.description: Application state transitions go through Messages and update.
prefs.question: Does this change use ModelRef.set, ModelRef.modify, or WritableProjection.set for an ordinary application Model transition instead of sending a Message through update?
prefs.guidance: Count only added or changed calls. Checkpoint installation, restoration, and reconciliation are allowed infrastructure uses because they install already-derived values. Ordinary domain behavior, including convenient local mutations, must go through a Message and update, normally using evo.

prefs.name: Unvalidated input use
prefs.description: Untrusted input is validated before it influences behavior.
prefs.question: Does this change add a path where untrusted input influences program behavior before crossing its declared validation or decoding boundary?
prefs.guidance: Count data received from clients, wire payloads, external providers, files, environment variables, or other trust boundaries. Passing a value directly into its validator or decoder is allowed; branching on it, using it in a lookup, persisting it, or passing it to business logic first is a violation. Judge only paths visible in added or changed code.

prefs.name: Authorization bypass
prefs.description: Protected effects cannot bypass capability or authorization checks.
prefs.question: Does this change add or alter a protected operation so its capability or authorization check can be skipped before the protected effect occurs?
prefs.guidance: Count a path only when the changed code shows a protected read, write, command, or external effect reachable without the required check. Do not infer missing authorization for operations that the diff does not identify as protected.

prefs.name: Internal failure leak
prefs.description: Public failures do not expose internal implementation details.
prefs.question: Does this change expose raw internal failure details across a public or client-facing boundary?
prefs.guidance: Count newly exposed stack traces, database or provider errors, queries, filesystem paths, secret configuration, or similarly internal details. Internal logging and deliberately defined public error codes or messages are allowed.

prefs.name: Restating comment
prefs.description: Comments explain non-obvious reasons or public contracts instead of narrating code.
prefs.question: Does this change add a comment or doc comment that only restates adjacent code, a symbol name, or a parameter name?
prefs.guidance: Count only comments added or changed in this review. Do not count concise public API documentation that states a contract not evident from the signature, or comments explaining a workaround, ordering constraint, rejected alternative, or other non-obvious reason.

prefs.name: Forwarding abstraction
prefs.description: New abstractions contribute behavior or a meaningful boundary.
prefs.question: Does this change add a wrapper or indirection module that only forwards to one existing operation without adding behavior, policy, translation, or an ownership boundary?
prefs.guidance: Count wrappers that pass arguments and results through unchanged, and modules whose only purpose is to re-export one other module. Do not count adapters that translate protocols or types, stable public entry points, dependency-injection boundaries, or wrappers that enforce policy.
